items.actClause: AN ACT to create a demonstration program and task force on teleworking
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6476

SPONSOR: GONZALEZ
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to create a demonstration program and task force on teleworking

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of the study is to determine whether telecommuting by
certain state employees could reduce state costs while improving the
work life of employees who have difficulty commuting, are unable to
commute, or who must commute long distances to their places of employ-
ment. The study would require that the results be presented in a report
eighteen months following the approval of this legislation.  The study
will attempt to identify possible employee candidates that can be chosen
to participate in an active telework pilot program while also identify-
ing the benefits of teleworking.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

The "Telework 2023 Act" shall establish a task force whose primary
responsibility shall be to produce a study of the possible use of tele-
commuting within New York's state agencies. This pilot program study
shall be conducted on the following State departments:  financial
services, health, transportation and the division of housing and commu-
nity renewal. The task force will consist of the departments of Environ-
mental Conservation, Transportation, Civil Service, Worker' Compen-
sation, General Services, and the Office of Advocate for Persons with
Disabilities. The task force will be chaired by a designee of the gover-
nor. The temporary president of the Senate and the Speaker of the Assem-
bly shall each appoint a liaison to the task force.

There will be two phases for this act. First, the task force and demon-
stration program will identify suitable employees. Phase two will study
the benefits and/or detriments of telework. The pilot program shall be
established for a period of 18 months. After that time, the demon-
stration programs study findings shall be combined into a final report
and presented to the Governor, and the Legislature and me made available
to the public.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation is a response to the growing practice of the use of
telework as a future method of occupation away from the principal place
of employment.

Telecommuting is being used more and more by businesses as a way to save
money for employers, allow more freedom for a balance between work and
family life for employees, reduce air pollution and traffic congestion,
reduce absenteeism, and especially to accommodate those who are disa-
bled. As a result of these reasons and more, telecommuting has a very
promising future as a form of out of the office work.

In light of its many benefits, teleworking requires further research to
move a step closer to using it as a way to save the New York State
taxpayer money, while also profiting the state and its employees.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Compensation for actual and necessary expenses of the task force

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the first of November next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become a law.

A.actClause: AN ACT directing a state agency telework report
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6476A

SPONSOR: GONZALEZ
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act directing a state agency telework report

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of the report is to determine how state agencies are allow-
ing their workers to telecornmute and the effects of telecommuting by
state workers. The study would require state agencies to submit informa-
tion on their official telecommuting policy as well as data on how many
workers and which job titles are eligible for telework.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Sets the title for this act, the "State Agency Telework
Report Act."

Section 2: Sets the legislative intent for this Act.

Section 3: Provides definitions for state agency and telework.

Section 4: Requires each agency to submit a telework report to the
Department of Civil Service by July 1, 2024 which includes specific data
on each agency's telework policy. In addition, employees can anonymously
submit their feedback on their agency's telework policy.  The DCS will
summarize and compile the data and report to the legislature by Septem-
ber 1, 2024.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation is a response to the growing practice of the use of
telework as a future method of occupation away from the principal place
of employment.

Telecommuting is being used more and more by state agencies, but little
information is publicly available to analyze the state's teleworking
policies for its workforce as well as the benefits and drawbacks of
telework.

This bill will allow policymakers to view and analyze the state's own
telework policies.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
